title: Byzantine Anno Mundi Calendar
intro: The Byzantine Anno Mundi calendar combines Julian month/day reckoning with an era and year start distinct from the Christian-era January year.
epoch: The conventional epoch is 1 September 5509 BCE in Julian reckoning. Anno Mundi means year of the world; it is a theological chronology, not a measured creation date.
structure: The year runs from September through August; month lengths and leap days follow Julian arithmetic.
example: 1 September 2026 Julian begins AM 7535; the preceding 31 August is still in AM 7534. The dates must be identified as Julian, not Gregorian.
history: Byzantine Christians used world-era reckoning in chronicles, religious and official dating.
model: For Julian years in the positive common-era range, add 5508 before September and 5509 from September onward. Conversion remains anchored to the underlying day coordinate.
limits: This is the Constantinopolitan convention; other medieval sources may use different world-era or year-start rules.
